question: How many offices of the University Grants Commission are in Delhi?
solution:
The correct answer is **2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The University Grants Commission (UGC) has **2 offices in Delhi**.
 
• The main office of the UGC is located at **Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, New Delhi**.
 
• The other office, known as the **South Campus office**, is located in the Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) complex, New Delhi.
 
• UGC is responsible for **coordination, determination, and maintenance of standards of university education** in India.
 
• It is a **statutory body** established under the UGC Act, 1956, and operates under the Ministry of Education, Government of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **University Grants Commission (UGC):**

 
 
• The UGC was established in 1956 and is headquartered in New Delhi.
 
• It provides recognition to universities in India and disburses funds to such recognized universities and colleges.
 
• It also ensures the maintenance of quality standards in higher education institutions.
 
 
 
• **Functions of UGC:**
 
 
• Promoting and coordinating university education.
 
• Determining and maintaining standards of teaching, examination, and research.
 
• Advising the Central and State governments on measures for the improvement of university education.
 
 
 
• **Importance of UGC:**
 
 
• Acts as a bridge between the government and higher education institutions.
 
• Ensures that institutions meet quality standards in education and research.
 
• Facilitates funding for development projects in universities and colleges.
 
 
 
• **Regional Offices of UGC:**
 
 
• UGC has regional offices across India, including in cities like Pune, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Bhopal, and Bengaluru, apart from its offices in Delhi.
 
• These regional offices cater to the needs of universities and colleges in their respective regions.
